title: Window to the world
text:
Before we discovered the KOMP device, I had long wished that just such a thing would come along and thanks to No Isolation, my wish eventually became reality.
If you are an elderly, or disabled person for whom using a PC, laptop or notebook for communications is difficult and for whom a mere telephone cannot provide the pleasure of face-to-face contact with friends and family, then KOMP is the answer.
Supremely simple and fuss free to use (no technical knowledge or experience required), the KOMP allows you to enjoy chats with loved ones at any time you wish as well as the possibility of seeing their photographs and receiving text messages on screen.
All of this is done on a high quality stand alone screen (very similar to a smallish TV).
When friends call, as long as you have the unit switched on you will hear a countdown tone for 10 beats along wit the name of whoever of your invited friends (no strangers can call you) then you will see them and be able to talk to them as a video call.
It’s simple, reliable, trouble free and great fun and it’s the perfect answer for maintaining contact without the hassle of computers, mobiles and other such devices.
I had one for my bedbound mum-in-law and I also have one for my own mum. Both families are great fans of the KOMP and during the current crisis it became even more essential than normal. Will would never want to be without this device and I cannot recommend it highly enough!

title: Fall detection? I call BS.
text:
I have my watch for multiple reasons. One of those being fall detection because I am a professional equestrian rider. I have fallen no less than a dozen times since purchasing my first watch with “fall detection.”

Most recently I have an Apple Watch Series 9. I have come off of a horse 3 times (HARD) while having this watch and none of those  times was there an emergency alert. However, I have clapped my hands excitedly for someone and also had a mild roll off of my body ball while stretching where my watch has gone off. What gives on when this thing registers? Do I have to pound my fist on the ground (if I’m conscious) after I’ve come off to get a fall to register? WTH Apple?

I realize that an accelerometer is the primary source that registers to tell the watch to make an emergency call, but Apple really should rethink their “fall detection.” 

My mother had several falls as an elderly obese person that were not registered. This was the absolute primary reason for the purchase. We had backup emergency buttons as well. 

I’ve had numerous hard hits to the ground from horses or otherwise and there has been no “fall” detected. 

I am well aware that this is not the end all be all in fall detection, but it fails nine times out of 10 in actual fall scenarios versus false positives for ridiculous everyday movements. 

Come on Apple, I know you can do better. I am absolutely happy to be a test subject for your fall detection upgrades since I continue to have many  instances in which it SHOULD register. 

My only saving grace is that, THANKFULLY,  the times I have come off, my cellular has worked. That is also a very sketchy issue. Cellular on the Apple Watch works at its own convenience.

title: This app carried me through one of the hardest seasons of my life
text:
I spent the last few years caring for my mom while she was living with stage 4 lung cancer. Nothing truly prepares you for how overwhelming caregiving becomes — emotionally, physically, and mentally. Every day felt like a juggling act: driving back and forth for chemotherapy, managing medications, updating advance medical directives, coordinating travel so she could see friends and family, scheduling physical therapy, managing oxygen equipment, dealing with insurance and deductibles, and trying to secure medical appointments months in advance.

It was exhausting. And often, it felt very lonely.

Caring Village brought calm and clarity into a situation that otherwise felt like constant chaos. The medication management section alone was a godsend — one less thing to keep in my head when I was already running on fumes. Having a shared calendar to coordinate tasks gave structure to days that felt overwhelming, and being able to communicate with the caregiver we hired in the later months — all in one place — made an enormous difference.

What mattered most was the peace of mind. Caring Village helped me feel supported, organized, and less alone at a time when everything felt heavy. It dramatically lowered my stress and allowed me to be more present with my mom, instead of constantly worrying about what I might be forgetting.

This app is clearly built by people who understand caregiving not as a checklist, but as a deeply human experience. I’m profoundly grateful it existed when I needed it most.

Thank you, Caring Village.

title: Bonnie S.
text:
I am a geriatric care manager and I discovered this app when I was trying to juggle communication among 30+ family members for one of my clients. I since have started several more “villages” for other clients and use most of the available options. Overall I love this app. I have the following observations to share in hopes it helps people make a decision about using this and also in hopes the developers are reading reviews

Pros: 
-ability to care plan and have staff document daily in the wellness journal to monitor compliance and communicate with family. 
-ability to message multiple people at once
-family and client ability to remain updated on status and keep all involved in the loop consistently 
-family ability to ask questions, send messages, add items to the calendar, etc. it promotes transparency among family, client and care team
-ability to use calendar to schedule staff and appointments. Also able to assign staff to tasks and ask for volunteer from family at times there is no staff in the home

Cons:
-friends can see most of what the inner circle sees. This poses a privacy issue for those not given authorization to see medical and clinical details. I have had to minimize information shared and can’t fully use the app in one of my cases
-inability to archive closed cases for future reference. They can only be deleted
-the care plan is only good for one day then disappears. From an agency perspective this limits our ability to do quality assurance and track trends
-notifications to email only link to the site but not the actual action it is notifying about so it takes extra time to locate what has been added
-inability to retract a message or edit
-support is quick to respond and helpful. However when I asked to whom I could direct my recommendations to I got no response. I’m hoping this review may get into the proper hands to address some of these suggestions for improvements 

Despite the “cons”,  have adopted used of this app for all of my clients receiving in-home care and feel it meets most of our needs.

Biggest issue is “friends” and “inner circle” can see almost everything. I was going to upload my dad’s medical cards, Medicare Card, etc, but realized friends and inner circle can see them as well. I find this very intrusive. There’s absolutely no need for anyone else to see private documents. Therefore, the cousins we invited had to be cancelled or revoked. My advice to the developers is to allow the administrators to pick and choose categories for each group type to see. For example, friends can only read Wellness Journal, and inner circle can see that plus a couple other categories such as meds, calendar, messages. Until this happens, we’re just keeping this between the siblings.

title: New Update Makes Adding Notes Painfully Slow Since 8.5.0
text:
I’ve been using the Omron app for a long time, and the usability took a major step backward starting with version 8.5.0. The “New Home Screen” update introduced a workflow change that makes adding notes significantly more difficult than before.

Previously, I could add a note directly from the main screen. Now, when I tap a reading, the app takes about 10 seconds to load — and it always loads the chart first. I don’t need the chart, and I don’t use the chart for adding notes, yet I’m forced to see it every single time I want to annotate a reading. After that delay, I have to scroll down to “See all measurements,” but the scrolling is laggy and often requires several swipes before the app responds. Only after selecting “See all measurements” can I scroll again, enable “Show notes,” and finally add a note. This is a clear usability regression.

This change affected me during a medically sensitive moment. I was recently hospitalized for a stroke, and I rely on the ability to quickly annotate readings when symptoms or stress occur. The new slow, chart‑first workflow made it harder to document an important reading in real time, which is unacceptable for a health‑tracking app.

Omron should restore the ability to add notes directly from the main screen or streamline the workflow. Users who depend on this app for real medical situations should not be forced to wait through delays, laggy scrolling, and an unnecessary chart just to record essential information.

If this workflow cannot be improved, I may need to switch to another app that supports my Omron monitor, because quick note‑taking is essential for my medical tracking.

title: Delayed Safety Notifications Defeat the Purpose of Life360
text:
What good is Life360 for parents if notifications that our children have arrived at or departed from a location can be delayed by 3–5 minutes? Parents rely on this app for safety, awareness, and peace of mind. A notification that arrives several minutes after our child has already left or arrived defeats the purpose of receiving that alert in the first place.

When it comes to our children’s safety, timing matters. Parents should not have to wonder whether their child has left school, arrived home, or reached another destination while waiting several minutes for Life360 to notify them.

Life360 needs to take this issue seriously. Location and arrival/departure notifications should be delivered as promptly as technically possible, with reliable background tracking and minimal delays. If there is a technical limitation causing these delays, the company needs to explain it clearly and address it.

Parents depend on this app for more than convenience. We depend on it for information that helps us look after our children. A family safety app should prioritize timely, reliable notifications. Please fix this issue.
